_doc: Segment-A trail map parameters. Every entry is {value, why}. load_config() strips the 'why'.

navmap_free_dilation_m.why: A pose counts as 'on the paved/nav-map area' if a FREE (254) PGM cell lies within this radius: absorbs the 0.1 m PGM quantisation and the ~0.3-0.5 m offset between a hand-held scanner and the walker's feet. Exit/entry moved by <1.2 m of path for 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 m (see segment.json dilation_sensitivity).

dilation_sensitivity_m.why: Report how the exit/entry depend on the dilation choice.

approach_m.why: Brief: ~10 m of approach on the paved area at each end.

work_margin_raw_m.why: Raw path length processed beyond exit/entry before cutting, so the 10 m approach is cut from an already cleaned line.

pause_min_step_m.why: Pause removal: a pose is kept only after the scanner moved >=0.2 m in XY (stationary jitter is a few cm; equals the station spacing).

loop_close_radius_m.why: Back-and-forth detection: returning within 1.0 m (about half a trail width) of an already kept point closes a loop.

loop_close_dz_m.why: Loop closure also needs |dz|<0.5 m so that vertically separated trail passes (switchbacks, bridges) are never merged; a person's scanner height varies <0.3 m between passes.

loop_min_arc_m.why: Only an excursion of >=2 m walked path (2x the closure radius) is a loop; normal forward walking never returns within 1 m after 2 m.

loop_max_arc_m.why: Upper bound on a removable excursion; the whole trail loop (~850 m) can never be pruned. Longest pruned excursion is reported.

smoothing_sigma_m.why: Gaussian smoothing along arc length removes walking sway (+-0.1 m at step frequency) but keeps bends of radius >~1.5 m.

station_spacing_m.why: Brief: resample at 0.2 m XY arc length (same as the existing map contract).

res_m.why: Brief and existing map contract: 0.1 m cells.

coverage_radius_m.why: Map content is kept within 12 m of the centreline (brief: >=10 m; BEV reaches 6 m ahead / 4 m sideways and sensors 8 m, from a robot up to 0.75 m + 0.35 m off-route before 'wrong-way' termination). Outside: known=0, unsupported, empty atlas.

crop_radius_m.why: Point crop radius around centreline AND raw walked poses: coverage 12 m + 2 m so neighbourhood filters (<=1.5 m) are not edge-biased inside the covered area.

bbox_margin_m.why: Dense grid = route bounding box + 12.5 m (coverage radius + 0.5 m).

layer_thickness_m.why: Lowest layer = lowest point with >= layer_min_points points within 5 cm above it in the cell (5 cm ~ 2-3 sigma of LiDAR range noise on hard ground).

layer_min_points.why: Rejects isolated single low returns (multipath/noise) while keeping sparse ground under vegetation (median density ~50 points per 0.1 m cell). No normal filter: the lowest return of a trunk/wall/riser column is its base, i.e. ground; provider normals are unreliable in vegetation.

vegetation_slab_m.why: Slab above the lowest layer used for the return-concentration test (grass/fern height scale).

bare_concentration_min.why: Bare soil/concrete: most returns in the 0.3 m slab lie in the lowest 5 cm. Below 0.5 the layer is diffuse (vegetation).

median_window.why: Pit/spike test identical to the old proxy (5x5 = 0.5 m median).

median_tolerance_m.why: Old proxy value; a 0.25 m deviation from the 0.5 m neighbourhood median is a pit/spike, not terrain (risers <=0.2 m pass).

envelope_radius_m.why: Lower-envelope cone radius (about half the robot length): object tops are judged against ground seen within 0.6 m.

envelope_slope_deg.why: Cone slope of the lower envelope: natural ground up to 45 deg (steeper than any supported grade) is not mistaken for an object top.

vegetation_top_min_m.why: A lowest layer >=0.25 m above the 45-deg envelope AND diffuse (concentration<0.5) is a vegetation/object top: ground there is unobserved (stays unknown unless within the 0.2 m gap fill).

connect_max_dz_m.why: Ground continuity: 8-neighbour steps up to 0.30 m (max riser 0.20 m + slope 45 deg over 0.1 m) connect cells into one surface grown from the walked path.

min_component_area_m2.why: Observed-ground islands not connected to the walked-path surface are kept only if >=1 m^2 (rejects isolated flat object tops such as rock/post tops).

interpolate_radius_m.why: Old proxy value: gaps up to 0.2 m are interpolated (nearest); larger gaps stay unknown/unsupported.

walked_cell_radius_m.why: Cells within 0.15 m of a moving raw pose are 'under the walked path' (scanner XY ~ foot position within a stride).

device_height_radius_m.why: Ground under a pose for the device-height estimate: median lowest layer within 0.2 m.

device_height_min_speed_mps.why: Pauses excluded: during long stops the operator lowered the scanner (h 0.3-1.2 m for 20-40 s at s=132, 351, 533, 649, 720 m).

prior_fill_under_path.why: Brief: ground under the walked path ~= scanner z - device height; used only for walked-path cells whose ground is otherwise unknown.

prior_tolerance_m.why: Walked-path seeds must lie within 0.5 m of scanner z - device height (~4 robust sigma of the measured device-height spread, 0.12 m).

second_layer_gap_m.why: A second surface layer in the same cell must start >= 0.3 m above the lowest one (distinct surface, not the same ground).

sub_surface_min_drop_m.why: The lowest layer is replaced by the walked-connected upper layer only if it lies >= 0.5 m below it (deeper than the 0.2 m step limit + ditch-edge effects); shallower differences are real terrain.

max_step_m.why: Stair-mode riser capability (brief default; TO BE CONFIRMED by the user). Measured as max |dz| to known neighbours within step_radius.

step_radius_m.why: Discontinuity = max |dz| to the 8 neighbours and axis central differences over +-0.1 m (0.2 m baseline): a riser smeared over two 0.1 m cells is still measured at full height, but only the cells on/straddling the edge are flagged (a 0.2 m dilation removed 0.2 m of usable tread beside every ditch). A 35 deg slope gives <= 0.14 m.

max_grade_deg.why: Max sustained grade (brief default; TO BE CONFIRMED).

grade_radius_m.why: Grade = least-squares plane over a 0.6 m disc (spans two 0.3 m stair treads, so single risers are averaged; a 1.0 m disc tilted the plane of a 1.1 m-wide tread towards an adjacent ditch/bank and removed ~0.5 m of usable tread).

trail_terrain_exemption.why: User statement (2026-11-16): all terrain along the walked trail is traversable in stair mode. Inside the trail zone, step/grade limits are not applied; they still apply everywhere else.

trail_zone_halfwidth_m.why: Trail zone = within 0.75 m of the raw walked path (the acceptance band is +-0.75 m; robot half-width 0.29 m + walker sway).

trail_zone_connect_max_step_m.why: Trail-zone cells must be reachable from the walked line through steps <= max_step, so ditches/ledges beside the trail are NOT exempted.

trail_zone_max_cross_grade_deg.why: Side slopes steeper than the grade limit across the trail direction are not trail terrain (not exempted).

body_band_m.why: Old proxy band: below 0.22 m = within stair-mode step capability (0.20 m + 2 cm ground noise); above 0.80 m = above the robot (Gemini camera at 0.64 m, body+sensors ~0.7 m, +0.1 m margin). Lower bound measured above the highest known ground in the 3x3 neighbourhood (riser/ledge faces are terrain, handled by the step test); upper bound above the cell's own ground.

body_min_points.why: Old proxy: >=2 returns in the body band of a 0.1 m column (single returns are noise).

vertical_normal_max_abs_nz.why: |normal_z|<0.35 (normal within ~20 deg of horizontal) = vertical surface (trunk, wall, post, rock face).

continuation_top_m.why: Continuation test = returns directly above the robot height (0.8-1.2 m) in the same 0.1 m column: trunks/posts/shrubs continue upward, grass does not; overhanging canopy higher than 1.2 m is ignored.

subbin_m.why: Body band split in 6 sub-bins (0.22-0.80 m) for the vertical-continuity test.

linear_structure_classes.why: Classification codes that are empirically thin vertical/linear structures along the trail (posts, handrails; see classes.json). Used only as HARD evidence, never to make anything soft.

pca_block_cells.why: Shape analysis in 0.3 x 0.3 m voxels, two voxels over the body band (0.22-0.51, 0.51-0.80 m): roughly isotropic boxes (trunk/post diameter scale), using true point x,y.

pca_min_points.why: Minimum returns per voxel for a covariance estimate; sparser voxels give no soft evidence (conservative).

linear_min.why: Linearity (l1-l2)/l1 >= 0.7 with a near-vertical main axis = post/trunk/pole.

vertical_axis_min_abs_z.why: Main axis within ~37 deg of vertical.

planar_min.why: Planarity (l2-l3)/l1 >= 0.5: a surface. With a near-horizontal normal = wall/rock face/trunk; with scatter < soft_min_scattering = any solid surface (rock top, bench, ledge).

vertical_plane_max_normal_z.why: Plane normal within ~17 deg of horizontal.

continuous_column_min_vertical_fraction.why: A column occupied in all 6 sub-bins, continuing above 0.8 m and with >=50% vertical normals is a solid upright (trunk/post/wall).

soft_min_scattering.why: Soft requires volumetric scatter l3/l1 >= 0.1 (not a surface or a line).

soft_requires_no_body_top_continuation.why: Conservative: anything that continues above the robot height (0.8-2.0 m) in the same column is hard (shrubs with woody stems, trunks).

halfwidth_m.why: Brief default: a person (shoulder ~0.45 m) physically passed within +-0.30 m of the raw scanner path.

apply_in_saved_map.why: map.npz layer 5/6 use the prior (variant c); variant b (no prior) is kept in aux.npz and reported.

source.value: raw 10 Hz poses inside segment A (incl. pruned back-and-forth)
source.why: The surveyor walked all of them.

width_clip_m.why: Brief: corridor width = measured feasible width clipped to [1,3] m; layer 3 = distance to centreline - width/2.

lateral_search_m.why: Feasible-width measurement: robot centre offsets within +-1.5 m (same as qualify_routes) at 0.05 m.

acceptance_band_m.why: Brief: continuous path must stay within +-0.75 m of the centreline.

fit_margin_m.why: User: report where feasible width < 0.58 m + 0.10 m margin.

dp_max_shift_per_station_m.why: Path search: lateral change <= 0.10 m per 0.2 m station (<= 27 deg off the route heading); extracted path is re-validated with fine + swept footprints using its own heading.

riser_min_m.why: A riser is a rise/fall >= 8 cm within ~0.1-0.3 m along the centreline profile (well above the ~1-2 cm ground noise, below any real stair riser 0.10-0.20 m).

riser_max_run_m.why: The rise must happen within 0.35 m along the route (a vertical-ish face, allowing an oblique crossing); slower rises are grade, not steps.

tread_max_m.why: Consecutive risers further apart than 1.2 m along the route belong to different flights.

min_risers.why: A flight needs >= 3 risers in the same direction.

sections.why: Cross-sections: deterministic picks from the old-proxy diagnosis (longest failing run per cause, narrowest lane, stairs) - listed in report.json.
